gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ so much cake — I feel sick now.
gaps.hint: past act with a present consequence
gaps.explanation: The regret is about a past action, so 'wish' takes the past perfect: had not eaten.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ me tonight, I will send you the files first thing.
gaps.explanation: A realistic future condition uses the present simple after 'if': email.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ taller, but genes are genes.
gaps.hint: an impossible present wish with were
gaps.explanation: For impossible present wishes, formal English uses 'were': were.

gaps.sentence: I will be surprised if he ___ on time for once.
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a real future condition takes the present simple: arrives.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ me, I would have helped you move house.
gaps.hint: a missed request in the past
gaps.explanation: An unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had asked.

gaps.sentence: If you had set an alarm, you ___.
gaps.explanation: The present result of a past unreal condition takes 'would not be': would not still be asleep.

gaps.sentence: If the battery is completely flat, the engine ___ at all.
gaps.explanation: A permanent characteristic takes the present simple in a zero conditional: does not start.
